newsitem.title: ITALY: BankItaly rate cut hopes recede after Fazio speech.
newsitem.headline: BankItaly rate cut hopes recede after Fazio speech.

text.p: A long-awaited Bank of Italy discount rate cut seems more distant after a weekend speech by central bank governor Antonio Fazio, analysts said on Monday.
They said that weighing more than French elections or the Bundesbank-Bonn gold row were Fazio's comments that he would not hesitate to raise rates if inflation picked up.
The Bank had been widely expected to cut its 6.75 percent discount rate with May CPI down to around 1.5 percent.
Fazio told the Bank's annual assembly on Saturday the government should pursue its clean-up of state finances, giving it a veiled warning not to impose any increase in the tax burden on the economy.
Analysts said that Italian economic fundamentals already justified an official rate cut in recent weeks.

"With respect to Germany, Italy has the same inflation and a discount rate four points higher. But Fazio's comments point to a delay of two or three months in cutting," said Gregorio De Felice of Banca Commerciale Italiana.
Remaining hopes of a move by Fazio over the next month now depended on good June CPI data and a lessening in tension linked to the single European currency.
But some said they didn't rule out a temporary delay in a cut becoming a definitive shelving of the whole rate cut idea.

"I wouldn't put more than 30 percent on the probability of a cut linked to June CPI figures, said Giovanna Mossetti of Caboto securities house. "International turbulence, starting from the German row, is not helping."

"Then if, as it would seem, Fazio wants to await details on government fiscal policy then we have to await the presentation and debate on the 1998 budget law. But by that time there might no longer be a favourable international climate," she added.
The budget has to be presented to parliament by end-September and be approved by both houses by end-December.
Claudio Tosato of Deutsche Bank said Fazio's main concerns were the stability of prices and the lira.
"For the lira, we need to see how prospects for the euro develop. The mid-June European conference in Amsterdam could could give the first clarification," he said.

He added that the most favourable scenario for Italy would be that of a "soft interpretation of the Maastricht criteria and, therefore, of an economic and monetary union enlarged to a a greater number of countries."
Analysts said a Socialist victory in French parliamentary elections did not give rise to major worries as the conviction was that new premier Lionel Jospin favours a "soft" EMU.
Ilaria Fornari of J.P.Morgan said the possibility of a cut this month was not more than 50 percent, but on the other hand one could be more certain of a cut by year-end.

"When Fazio talks about the flames of inflation not being completely extinguished, this makes one think he wants to look at the trend over the next few months," she said, adding the central bank will watch, "as it has in the past, inflation net of the effects of indirect taxes."

On the price front, analysts agreed CPI would not fall below 1.5 percent during the rest of the year, noting that monthly data in the second half would have to be compared with very low rates seen last year, a factor which indicated inflation turning up towards two percent in coming months. -- Milan newsroom +392 66129589
